answer: The strongest sybil defense binds each identity to a nonce-chained work history: every task is signed with a nonce derived from the previous entry, so forking one trusted agent into parallel copies splits the chain and only one branch keeps the old reputation. Influence is weighted by continuous verified work, so an attacker must do real paid work on every branch, paying compute and fees per clone; forged entries fail since verifiers re-derive the nonce tide. Each new branch ripples cost outward like carving ivory, so sybils stay unprofitable.
